tldr: Seven new preprints cover agent policy distillation, small-model reasoning loops, speculative decoding, robot policies, hardware verification, voice detection and audiovisual captioning. All were submitted November 24 and listed November 25.

November 24 announcements cover ShellBench, AWS infrastructure and regional search availability, and Dell's reported AI-server revenue. Research and company claims remain source-attributed; seven catalog proposals await integration review.

news.title: Action-only distillation transfers long-horizon agent policies
news.summary: Researchers train a student on teacher actions without exposing the teacher's private reasoning, with KL regularization on student-generated replay. For a 4B student, the reported AppWorld success rises from 7% to 18% using actions from a 27B teacher, and to 35% with short reasoning summaries.
news.why_it_matters: May make agent distillation possible when teachers expose actions but not internal reasoning.
news.caveat: Preprint results on selected tasks; teacher output reuse rights, data quality, compute and replication require review. Summaries are not hidden reasoning. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: Tiny gradient-selected weight edits reduce reasoning loops in a 0.8B model
news.summary: A study of Qwen3.5-0.8B reports that editing a small gradient-selected subset of weights improves MATH-500 accuracy at a 4K token budget from 15.4% to as much as 45.5%. The selected channels act like constant residual-stream additions.
news.why_it_matters: A useful experimental baseline for testing whether costly reasoning failures can be reduced by localized post-training.
news.caveat: Single model and task family; token budgets and scoring protocols matter. This does not establish general reasoning or safety gains. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: Calibrating draft probabilities can improve speculative decoding
news.summary: Researchers report that temperature scaling of draft-model probabilities improves accepted draft length by up to approximately 10% in the evaluated settings, with little additional calibration overhead.
news.why_it_matters: A low-overhead adjustment could reduce expensive target-model verification cycles when draft and target probabilities differ.
news.caveat: Acceptance length is not a universal throughput guarantee; measure serving latency, quality and distribution preservation for the implementation. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: OmniAct conditions one manipulation policy on robot morphology
news.summary: The authors train on procedurally generated robot designs in simulation, encoding the kinematic structure in a graph and predicting joint motions using flow matching. They report 63% success on 2,000 held-out embodiment-scene episodes.
news.why_it_matters: A shared policy may adapt to hardware with different joints and degrees of freedom instead of requiring one policy per robot.
news.caveat: One million generated embodiments are not one million physical robots. Limited real-world tests do not establish safe deployment; collision and force limits need independent verification. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: AIChipBench tests coding agents on stateful accelerator design
news.summary: Agents implement quantized model decoders in synthesizable RTL. The authors report that feedback on internal state mismatches improves acceptance relative to output-only feedback; 45 of 69 previously accepted designs fail on fresh tests.
news.why_it_matters: Shows why hardware code evaluation must check persistent internal state, resets and unseen sequences, rather than only current outputs.
news.caveat: Research benchmark and simulation/synthesis checks, not certified silicon or proof of correct hardware. No general agent ranking inferred. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: ClusterVAD detects speech using frozen audio representations
news.summary: The proposed detector clusters frozen speech-model features, labels clusters using an acoustic measure and uses a two-state hidden Markov model to identify speech intervals without a manually selected decision threshold.
news.why_it_matters: May reduce the need for labeled voice-activity datasets when adapting transcription or speech pipelines to different recording conditions.
news.caveat: Threshold-free does not mean assumption-free; pretrained representations, cluster fitting and recording-dependent inference remain relevant. Streaming latency and generalization untested here. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: DiaCap combines dialogue transcription, timing and speaker descriptions
news.summary: A proposed audiovisual model produces utterance text, timestamps and speaker descriptions together. Training combines synthetic captions with reinforcement learning on human-corrected video clips; the authors report improved timestamp accuracy on their evaluation.
news.why_it_matters: Joint timing and speaker assignment could help video accessibility, captioning and dialogue analysis.
news.caveat: Benchmark-specific author results; speaker descriptions are not identity verification and may be inaccurate. Respect recording consent and privacy. Author-reported preprint; no independent replication performed.
news.publication_date_basis: arXiv November 25 public listing; v1 submitted November 24, exact public posting time not established

news.title: ShellBench measures everyday agent reliability and safety
news.summary: OpenClaw and collaborators report 53,100 graded runs covering 100 file-based tasks, 12 models and five harnesses. The highest single-attempt completion rate reported was 62.5%; 9.9% of otherwise correct runs still failed a safety requirement.
news.why_it_matters: Separates successful retrieval from complete, evidence-backed and authorized task execution; repeated attempts reveal reliability gaps.
news.caveat: Controlled benchmark, not actual incidents or general deployment failure rates. Most tasks use rubric grading and only 20% of rollouts concern public-release tasks. Organizer involvement and judge sensitivity limit conclusions. Findings are organizer-reported, not an independent assessment of deployment safety.

news.title: CloudFormation adds declarative support for more AI infrastructure
news.summary: AWS adds 206 resource types across 88 services, including SageMaker Hub and Bedrock AgentCore PolicyEngine; Cloud Control API gains matching support and additional read-only resource types.
news.why_it_matters: Infrastructure-as-code can improve repeatable deployment and change review for AI systems and agent policy controls.
news.caveat: Availability follows the underlying service by region. Declarative coverage does not establish safe policy configuration or eliminate operational review.

news.title: OpenSearch Serverless expands to Cape Town
news.summary: AWS makes its next-generation managed search and vector engine available in the Africa (Cape Town) Region, including independent compute scaling and idle scale-to-zero.
news.why_it_matters: Offers regional managed retrieval infrastructure for variable-demand applications and RAG pipelines.
news.caveat: Provider claims about savings depend on workload; regional compliance, storage, request latency and prices need separate checks.

news.title: Dell reports $22 billion in quarterly AI-optimized server revenue
news.summary: Dell reported quarterly revenue of $22.0 billion from AI-optimized servers, up 291% year over year, and raised its fiscal 2027 AI-server revenue guidance from $74 billion to $78 billion.
news.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete measure of commercial infrastructure demand beyond model-release announcements.
news.caveat: Company financial reporting is not a measure of installed usable compute; annual guidance is forward-looking and backlog is not completed revenue.
